thread:
incident-bot: P0 ALERT — spike in 5xx errors for /v1/generate (prod). Alerting oncall now. Link: https://alerts.redwood/alerts/1792001234 :rotating_light:

alice wong: I got paged, joining. Seeing error rate ~18% on production last 5m.

benji rao: I'm online, checking infra metrics (k8s/gpu nodes) and LB errors.

carmen lopez: War room: https://meet.redwood/warroom/1792001234 — created and pinned.

alice wong: Owner: alice wong (runtime) for triage. Benji infra, Carmen SRE for mitigations, Sarah for status page/customer comms.

oncall-pager: Confirmed page delivery to alice wong and benji rao :white_check_mark:

alice wong: Quick triage: reproduce locally against canary — getting `500` with stack trace reference to kv cache eviction. Dumping recent logs:
```
2026-03-15T14:02:11Z ERROR handler.go:124 request_id=abcd1234 err="kv cache miss + OOM?"
2026-03-15T14:02:12Z WARN runtime.go:88 layer=attention kernel_latency_ms=240
```

benji rao: Infra looks healthy: nodes ok, no pod restarts, autoscaler not triggered. LB shows upstream 502->500 conversion around 14:01 UTC. Could be model runtime degradation.

carmen lopez: Mitigation plan: 1) divert traffic to earlier model variant (v1.2) with fallback policy, 2) scale a small set of warm instances with increased kv cache, 3) if needed, enable circuit-breaker to reduce retries. Who can flip traffic?

alice wong: I can kick the rollback to v1.2 for the affected route. Will do a canary first with 5% traffic.

matthew t: I'll prepare the status page copy. Draft below, please edit: 
"We are investigating elevated error rates for the /v1/generate endpoint impacting some customers. Our engineering team has identified a runtime degradation and is rolling back to a stable model variant while we continue investigating. No data exposure is suspected. Next update in 15 minutes."

sarah k: Good. Add CI impact note: "Some requests may experience 500 errors or increased latency. Tenant-specific retries may amplify failures for high-throughput clients."

alice wong: Rolling canary now to v1.2 (5% traffic) -> watching logs.

incident-bot: Canary rollout started: route=/v1/generate percent=5 variant=v1.2

alice wong: Canary looks good for 3 minutes, error rate down from 18% -> 3% on canary cohort. Proceeding to 30% in 2m.

benji rao: FYI I increased node KV cache config on the warm pool (temporary) per runbook step 3. Command run: `kubectl set env deployment/runtime KV_CACHE_SIZE=2G --namespace=production`

carmen lopez: Posting status page now. Sarah, can you post customer notification draft to #marketing-ops for visibility?

sarah k: Posted draft in #marketing-ops and tagged legal. Draft: 
"Dear customer, we are experiencing increased errors on /v1/generate. We are rolling back to a stable model variant to mitigate impact. No customer data is believed to be exposed. We will provide updates every 15 minutes. For urgent support, please contact support@redwood.com"

matthew t: I'll post the interim status on status.redwood.com -> Component: Generation API -> Status: Degraded Performance -> Body: using my draft + Sarah's additions.

alice wong: Increasing to 30% rollout -> monitoring. If error rate across all cohorts drops under 5% we can complete to 100%.

benji rao: Infra logs show KV eviction spikes at 14:00 correlating with higher model mem usage. Looks like a memory pressure/GC event in the runtime.

carmen lopez: Action items: 
- alice wong: finish rollback and confirm endpoint stability (owner)
- benji rao: capture heap/profile and open runtime bug (owner)
- sarah k: publish status and customer comms (owner)
- matthew t: coordinate updates and exec notify if >30m (owner)

alice wong: Completed 100% rollout to v1.2 at 14:12 UTC. Error rate down to baseline ~0.5% across prod.

incident-bot: Incident state change: Mitigation in progress -> Observed improvement.

matthew t: Posting update to status page: "Mitigation in progress, error rates reduced, rolling back to stable variant. Next update in 15 minutes or earlier."

sarah k: Sent customer notification to the affected tenant list and support channel. Copy pasted below for records: 
"Customer Notification: We observed elevated 500 errors on /v1/generate starting at ~14:00 UTC. Our engineers identified a runtime issue and rolled traffic back to a stable model variant (v1.2). Service levels are returning to normal. We will follow up with an incident report and RCA. If you have questions, contact support@redwood.com."

benji rao: Captured heap profiles and uploaded to S3: s3://redwood-incident-dumps/1792001234/heap.tar.gz. Creating runtime bug: RUNTIME-4572 with logs and profile.

carmen lopez: Let's keep updates cadence to 15m until we are stable for 30m. If stable, we'll move to triage and RCA.

sarah k: A note on comms: keep language conservative on exposure, avoid implying data loss. Legal ok with current wording.

matthew t: Exec notify rule triggered? If incident >30m and P0 we should cc CTO + CCO. We're at ~20m now, will prepare escalation pack if extends.

alice wong: Confirmed current owner handoff at 14:40 UTC to sarah k and benji rao for followup/closure. I'll remain available.

sarah k: Taking over coordination and will send final update when we enter post-incident state.

benji rao: I'll run the RCA timeline and include metrics, heap profiles, and timeline notes. Target preliminary RCA in 48 hours.

incident-bot: Incident timeline note added. Severity: P0 -> Mitigated (monitoring).

sarah k: Final internal note to include in incident report: "Root cause: memory pressure in runtime causing KV cache thrashing leading to increased 5xx. Immediate mitigation: rollback to v1.2 and temporary KV cache increase; next steps: runtime memory fixes and improved canary checks."

alice wong: Thanks team. Closing war room in 10m unless new regressions appear. :thumbsup:

sarah k: Closing note posted. I'll draft the post-incident customer follow-up and share in #incidents for review.
